gaps.quote: The paper shows $N<2L_{\rm b}$, so $s_{\rm b}<W_{\rm b}R$.
gaps.note: The inequality is reversed and the conclusion does not follow. With s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b, s_b < W_b R holds exactly when N > 2L_b; N < 2L_b would give s_b > W_b R. The paper (lines 1107-1109, L_b/N = 100/539 < 1/2; line 1167, 'Its deficit from W_b m is N-2L_b>0') shows N > 2L_b. Correct statement: the paper shows N>2L_b, so s_b<W_b R.

gaps.term: any invertible linear transformation costs O(V)
gaps.quote: Any invertible linear transformation of $H$ or $D$ costs $O(V)$ (cited)
gaps.note: Overstated. The paper (Lemma matrix-shear proof, lines 1425-1430) only claims that a lower triangular transformation of H or D costs O(V), via updating coordinates in descending physical order using earlier coordinates. The page's own justification ('Update coordinates from last to first, so each becomes a fixed combination of earlier ... coordinates') works only for lower-triangular maps, not arbitrary invertible ones. It also needs the diagonal entries to be units mod q^b. The page also does not say what the cited result states beyond the cost.

gaps.term: tape order of H before D
gaps.note: The linear-cost claim for these updates needs every H field to come before every D field in tape order, so each update writes a later field from an earlier one. The paper's Lemma matrix-shear (lines 1394-1410) assumes 'every H_i before every D_j' and notes (around line 1444) that the first and last updates 'target a later field controlled by an earlier field'. The page never states this hypothesis, so the reader cannot check that the additions are O(V) work.

gaps.quote: So $q$ divides no numerator or denominator of the finitely many matrices used.
gaps.note: Does not follow from the preceding sentences, which only require q not to divide denominators so that mu*xi^{-1} makes sense mod q^b. The paper (lines 1415-1421) chooses q to avoid every denominator in the finite table and every numerator of a diagonal entry of an invertible factor, so the triangular factors stay invertible mod q^b. The page does not say why numerators matter, and it states the condition for all numerators, which is wider than the paper requires.

gaps.quote: The network's rank budget, which counts dimension changes along its edges
gaps.note: The identity s_b = W_b R - N + 2L_b is asserted without the construction behind it. The page never says which matrix sits on each edge (a difference of projection matrices at the head and tail vertices, with rank equal to the dimension change), what dimension labels the vertices carry, or why decreasing edges contribute 2L_b. The reader cannot check the formula from what the page gives.

gaps.quote: the number of negative source projections
gaps.note: The page does not explain what a negative source projection is (a source matrix -P_U assigned to an input node, per the paper's rational matrix interface), and the linear-network page covers only sources and sinks of a route, not projections or edge matrices. 'Dimension lost on decreasing edges' is likewise unexplained.

gaps.quote: which the recurrence turns into a saving of a power of the chunk width
gaps.note: The page refers to 'the recurrence' without stating it. The paper (lines 1536-1560, equation swap-recurrence) uses F_0=O(1), F_k <= (s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), whose geometric sum gives time O(V e^tau) for chunk length e=m^k when s/W < m^tau. The reader cannot see how 'fewer than R interchanges per wire' yields a power saving.
